correctness.rationale: The classical boundary-format degree is D=(N+1)!/(product k_j!). Legendre's formula gives the displayed exact prime-adic valuation after using N=sum k_j. The digit-sum excess is zero exactly for carry-free base-p addition. For p=2, carry-free positive decompositions correspond bijectively to set partitions of the one-bit support of N; uniqueness of binary expansion makes the bijection exact and gives the Stirling count. The checker independently enumerates integer partitions, computes factorial degrees, valuations, and carry conditions.

value.rationale: Boundary-format hyperdeterminants are the determinant-like edge of Segre duality and occur as coisotropic or Chow forms. The theorem gives a complete and easily testable arithmetic classification of when their projective degree avoids a prime, and for parity it counts all odd-degree tensor formats at fixed largest dimension and number of factors exactly by a classical combinatorial invariant. This is a family-level structural statement rather than an isolated congruence or table recomputation.
